headline: 207 caps, 125 goals: Lionel Messi retires from international football
summary: The Argentine legend ends a historic 20-year career with the national team, leaving behind a record-breaking legacy of World Cup and Copa América glory.
details: Lionel Messi has officially retired from international football, ending a historic 20-year journey with the Argentina national team.
The 39-year-old superstar made a record 207 appearances for his country, scoring 125 goals and securing his place as Argentina's leading appearance-maker and goalscorer.
His international career was crowned by the 2022 FIFA World Cup victory in Qatar and two Copa América titles, completing one of the most decorated careers in football history.
FIFA President Gianni Infantino paid tribute to Messi, calling his career "extraordinary" and praising his magical talent and humility that will be remembered forever.
Messi's final international match was Argentina's defeat to Spain in the 2026 FIFA World Cup final.
Despite retiring from the national team, Messi will continue his club career with Inter Miami in the United States.
Messi's farewell message, written across three pages, emotional farewell to his teammates, family, and fans worldwide.
caption:
207 matches, 125 goals, and a World Cup trophy. The era of Lionel Messi with Argentina is officially over.

Lionel Messi has officially retired from international football, ending a historic 20-year journey with the Argentina national team.

The 39-year-old superstar made a record 207 appearances for his country, scoring 125 goals and securing his place as Argentina's leading appearance-maker and goalscorer.

His international career was crowned by the 2022 FIFA World Cup victory in Qatar and two Copa América titles, completing one of the most decorated careers in football history.

FIFA President Gianni Infantino paid tribute to Messi, calling his career "extraordinary" and praising his magical talent and humility that will be remembered forever.

Messi's final international match was Argentina's defeat to Spain in the 2026 FIFA World Cup final.

Despite retiring from the national team, Messi will continue his club career with Inter Miami in the United States.

Messi's farewell message, written across three pages, emotional farewell to his teammates, family, and fans worldwide.

headline_marked: [[Gas supply to normalize by September second week]], hopes BNP's Rizvi
headline: Gas supply to normalize by September second week, hopes BNP's Rizvi
summary: BNP acting secretary general Ruhul Kabir Rizvi says normal gas supply across the country will be restored by early September.
details: BNP acting secretary general Ruhul Kabir Rizvi expressed hope that normal gas supply across the country would be restored by the first or second week of September.
Rizvi stated that there are also signs that electricity supply will be improved. He made these comments during the party's 48th founding anniversary celebrations at Zia Udyan.

He attributed the current power and energy crisis to global factors, including the US-Iran conflict and disruptions to fuel-carrying vessels through the Strait of Hormuz, rather than internal government failure.
According to Rizvi, the government has allocated an additional Tk 40,000 crore for the power and energy sectors to address the crisis.
He also noted that a technical fault at the LNG terminal in Maheshkhali has been repaired and regasification has resumed.
Rizvi emphasized that the government is showing sincerity in tackling the crisis and working to fulfill election pledges, such as the Farmers' Card and Family Card.
Regarding the party's role, he stated that while the party and government have separate roles, the responsibility for running the country rests with the BNP and its alliance.
caption:
Will the gas crisis end soon? BNP's Ruhul Kabir Rizvi expects normal supply by the second week of September.

BNP acting secretary general Ruhul Kabir Rizvi expressed hope that normal gas supply across the country would be restored by the first or second week of September.

Rizvi stated that there are also signs that electricity supply will be improved. He made these comments during the party's 48th founding anniversary celebrations at Zia Udyan.

He attributed the current power and energy crisis to global factors, including the US-Iran conflict and disruptions to fuel-carrying vessels through the Strait of Hormuz, rather than internal government failure.

According to Rizvi, the government has allocated an additional Tk 40,000 crore for the power and energy sectors to address the crisis.

He also noted that a technical fault at the LNG terminal in Maheshkhali has been repaired and regasification has resumed.

Rizvi emphasized that the government is showing sincerity in tackling the crisis and working to fulfill election pledges, such as the Farmers' Card and Family Card.

Regarding the party's role, he stated that while the party and government have separate roles, the responsibility for running the country rests with the BNP and its alliance.
